sentences.text: Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Kaushlendra Singh,Rashmi Singh Hon'ble Rajeev Misra,J.

Heard Mr. Mohd. Kalim, the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A. for State and Mr.
Asgar Ahmad Siddiqui, Advocate holding brief of Mr. Kaushlendra Singh, the learned counsel representing first informant.

This application for bail has been filed by applicant Sameer seeking his enlargement on bail in Case Crime No.349 of 2023, under Sections 363, 366, 376 IPC and Section 4(2) Pocso Act, police station Deoband, district Saharanpur, during the pendency of trial.
Perused the record.

sentences.text: 1 Record shows that in respect of an incident which is alleged to have occurred on 14.06.2023, a prompt first information report dated 14.06.2023 was lodged by first informant, namely, Waseema (mother of the prosecutrix) and was registered as Case Crime No.0349 of 2023, under Section 363 IPC, police station Deoband, district Saharanpur.
In the aforesaid F.I.R., applicant Sameer has been nominated as solitary named accused.
The gravamen of the allegations made in the first information report is to the effect that named accused enticed away the minor daughter of the first informant, namely, X aged about 13 years.
After aforesaid first information report was lodged, Investigating Officer proceeded with statutory investigation of concerned case crime number in terms of Chapter XII CrPC.

The statement of the prosecutrix was recorded under Section 161 CrPC, which is on record at page 23 of the paper book,
wherein she has stated that she herself accompanied the applicant and thereafter by extending false promise of marriage, the applicant is alleged to have dislodged the modesty of the prosecutrix.
Thereafter, the prosecutrix was requested for her internal medical examination.
In her statement before the Doctor, who medically examined her, the prosecutrix has rejoined her previous statement recorded under Section 161 CrPC.
However, the Doctor who medically examined the prosecurix did not find any signs on her body so as to denote commission of sexual assault.

However, with regard to the private part of the prosecutrix, the Doctor has opined as follows :-
"Hymen - Torn, but no fresh bleeding seen."
Ultimately, the statement of the prosecutrix was recorded under Section 164 CrPC, which is on record at page 8 of the supplementary affidavit filed in support of bail application.
The prosecutrix in her aforesaid statement has improved upon her earlier statement under Section 161 CrPC and the statement given before the Doctor.

During the course of investigation, Investigation Officer also examined the first informant and other witnesses under Section 161 CrPC, who have substantially supported the F.I.R. On the basis of above and other material collected by the Investigating Officer during the course of investigation
, he came to the conclusion that offence under Sections 366 and 376 IPC and Section 4(2) Pocso Act is also made out against the applicant in the commission of crime in question.
He, accordingly, submitted the charge-sheet dated 24.07.2023, whereby applicant has been charge-sheeted under Sections 363, 366, 376 IPC and Section 4(2) Pocso Act.
The present application for bail came up for orders on 22.08.2023 and this Court passed the following order :-

" 1. Heard Mr. Mohd. Kalim, the learned counsel for applicant and the learned A.G.A.
for State.
2. Supplementary affidavit filed by the learned counsel for applicant in Court today, is taken on record.

3. At the very outset, the learned A.G.A. submits that the provisions of the POCSO Act have been invoked against the applicant only on the basis of the statement of Sameer vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104464066/
2 Principal of the institution from where the prosecutrin had studied Class-VIII.

He,

sentences.text: 4. In view of above, the Chief Medical Officer, Saharanpur is directed to conduct the radiological test/ossification test of the prosecturix for determining her age.
The age determination report shall be submitted before this Court on or before 13.09.2023.

5. In the meantime, the Investigating Officer, after taking permission of the Court in terms of Section 173(8) Cr.P.C., in case, the charge sheet has been submitted, will conduct further investigation regarding any material pertaining to the age of the prosecutrix in consonance with the provisions contained in Section 94 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015.

sentences.text: The copy of the supplementary CD be also transmitted to this Court before the next date fixed.
6. Matter shall accordingly re-appear for orders as fresh on 13.09.2023."
In compliance of the above order dated 22.08.2023, learned A.G.A. has filed a compliance affidavit in Court today, which is taken on record.
Along with this compliance affidavit, a report of the Chief Medical Officer, Saharanpur regarding the age of the prosecutrix has also been appended.
As per the said document, the age of the prosecutrix is reported to be about 18 years.
Learned counsel for the applicant contends that even though the applicant is a named and charge-sheeted accused yet he is liable to be enlarged on bail.
Inviting the attention of the Court to the material brought on record, he submits that the prosecutrix is major as she is aged about 18 years as per the medical opinion.
Referring to the statement of the prosecutrix as recorded under Section 161 CrPC, he submits that the prosecutrix is a willing and consenting party.

In view of above,
no offence as complained of can be said to have been made by the applicant.
The prosecutrix and the applicant were in love with each other as is clearly explicit from her statement under Section 161 CrPC.
The prosecutrix in her subsequent statement under Section 164 CrPC has departed from her previous statement referred to above.
The embellishment, contradiction and exaggeration that has emerged in the subsequent statement of the prosecutrix as noted above remains unexplained up to this stage.

To buttress his submission he has referred to the judgement of the Supreme Court in Phool Singh Vs. State of M.P. (2022) 2 SCC 74 and on basis whereof it is contended by the learned counsel for applicant that conviction of an accused for an offence of rape and sexual assault can be maintained in the absence of medical evidence and on the solitary statement of the prosecutrix.
However, in such a circumstance the statement of the prosecutrix should be clear, categorical and consistent.

sentences.text: When the aforesaid test is applied to the facts of the present case and the statements of the prosecutrix referred to above are examined as a whole then they do not fall in the category of impeccable evidence and therefore un-worthy of reliance.
He, therefore, submits that no prosecution of the applicant can be maintained on the basis of above.
Even otherwise, the applicant is a man of clean antecedents having no criminal history to his credit except the present one.
The applicant is in jail since 15.06.2023.

As such, he has undergone more than three months of Sameer vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104464066/

sentences.text: The police report under Section 173(2) CrPC has already been submitted against the applicant, therefore the entire evidence sought to be relied upon by the prosecution against applicant stands crystalized.
However, up to this stage, no such circumstance has emerged necessitating the custodial arrest of applicant during the pendency of trial.
It is thus contended that applicant is liable to be enlarged on bail.
In case the applicant is enlarged on bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall co-operate with the trial.
Per contra, the learned A.G.A. and the learned counsel representing first informant have vehemently opposed the prayer for bail.
They submit that the modesty of the prosecutrix has been dislodged by the applicant by extending false promise of marriage.
There is nothing on record to show up to this stage that applicant has solemnized marriage with the prosecutrix.
Considering the tender age of the prosecutrix and the false promise extended by the applicant they submit that no indulgence be granted by this court in favour of the applicant.

To buttress their submissions, they have relied upon the judgements of the Supreme Court in Pramod Suryabhan Pawar Vs. State of Maharashtra 2019 SCC OnLine SC 1073; Maheshwar Tigga Vs. State of Jharkhand (2020) 10 SCC 108; Sonu alias Subhash Kumar Vs. State of U.P. 2021 SCC OnLine SC 181; Mandar Deepak Pawar Vs. The State of Maharashtra and Another 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 649 and Naim Ahmed Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), 2023 SCC OnLine SC 89 and on the basis thereof they submit that no sympathy be shown by this Court in favour of the applicant.

sentences.text: Having heard the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A. for State, the learned counsel representing first informant, upon perusal of material brought on record, nature and gravity of offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, accusation made, coupled with the fact that as per the medical opinion the prosecutrix is aged about 18 years, prima facie the prosecutrix is major, there is nothing on record to show that the prosecutrix was abducted or kidnapped by the applicant, to the contrary the prosecutrix is a willing and consenting party, absence of any injury on the body of the prosecutrix clearly goes to show that there was no forcible commission of sexual assault, it clearly denotes the consent of the prosecurix in having physical relations with the applicant, it is an undisputed fact that the prosecutrix and the applicant were in love with each other for two and half years, the prosecutrix in her subsequent statement recorded under Section 164 CrPC has departed from her earlier statement recorded under Section 161 CrPC, the embellishment, contradiction and exaggeration appearing in the subsequent statement of the prosecutrix as noted above remains unexplained up to this stage, the prosecutrix in her aforesaid statement has narrated a story which is totally alien to her previous statement under Section 161 CrPC, the police report under Section 173 (2) CrPC has already been submitted, therefore the entire evidence sought to be relied upon by the prosecution against applicant stands crystalized, but in spite of above the learned A.G.A. nor the learned counsel representing first informant could point out any such circumstance from the record necessitating the custodial arrest of the applicant during the pendency of trial, judgement of the Apex Court in the case of Sumit Subhashchandra Gangwal and Another Vs. State of Maharashtra and Another 2023 LiveLaw (SC) 373 (paragraph 5), the clean antecedents of the applicant, the period of incarceration undergone, but without making any comments on the merit of the case, the applicant has made out a case for bail.

Let the applicant Sameer, involved in aforesaid case crime number, be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice :-
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the date fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.

In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under section 229-A I.P.C.
(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under section 82 Cr.P.C., may be issued and if applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation

,
then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law,
under section 174-A I.P.C.
(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under section 313 Cr.P.C. If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
(v) The trial court may make all possible efforts/endeavour and try to conclude the trial within a period of one year after the release of the applicant.
However, it is made clear that any wilful violation of above conditions by the applicant, shall have serious repercussion on his bail so granted by this court and the trial court is at liberty to cancel the bail, after recording the reasons for doing so, in the given case of any of the condition mentioned above.
Order Date :- 19.9.2023.
Rks.
